116	| ...                                                          |
117	+--------------------------------------------------------------+

121	       make the gate pass: (a) wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto

123	       gate exempts intentional scroll containers); or (b) switch to a

136	Powers:    [ power meters ]                   [ ability badges ]
137	Missions:  [ list of deployments + result badges ]
138	Edit:      [ schema form: name, alias, class(select), power(number),

145	## Build guidelines
146	
147	Component map (region -> spartan primitive):
148	
149	- Navigation rail: `hlm-sidebar` and its parts (`HlmSidebarMenu*`, `HlmSidebarGroup*`, trigger, rail). Let it own its mobile off-canvas behaviour.
150	- Top bar controls: `hlmBtn` (icon buttons), `hlmInput` (search), `hlm-tooltip` on icon-only buttons, `hlm-avatar` for the account chip.
151	- Stat tiles and hero cards: `hlm-card` and its parts; `hlm-badge` for trends and classes; `hlm-avatar` for hero portraits.
152	- Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.
153	- Detail: `hlm-tabs`, `hlm-avatar`, `hlm-badge`; the edit form uses `hlm-field` + `hlm-label` + `hlmInput` + `hlm-select` + `hlm-switch` + a textarea; retire uses `hlm-dialog`. Toast/feedback via whatever spartan provides (sonner/toast) or a small local one.
154	- Icons everywhere via `<ng-icon>` per the scheme above.
155	
156	MVVM (the house pattern, enforced):
157	
158	- Each routed feature screen (Dashboard, Roster, HeroDetail, Recruit) gets a ViewModel: an `@Injectable` service holding all logic and state as signals, unit-testable with no DOM.
159	- The component lists its VM in its own `providers: [XViewModel]` (component-scoped, NOT `providedIn: 'root'`), injects it, and binds the template to `vm` signals. The component class stays thin: no business logic, no `.subscribe`, state lives in the VM.
160	- Presentational pieces (hero card, stat tile, power meter) live under `src/app/ui/`, take `input()`/`output()`, inject no data service.
161	- Forms are schema-driven with zod (the existing house pattern): a zod schema is the single source of truth, the model is `z.infer<typeof schema>`, validation flows through `validateStandardSchema`, no per-field validators, no reactive or template-driven forms.
162	
163	Responsive rules (the build MUST satisfy the Part 5 gate at 375 / 768 / 1280):
164	
165	- No horizontal page scroll at any breakpoint. Reach for the layout grammar: `grid` for regions with responsive column counts (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`), `flex` with `flex-wrap` for button rows, never fixed pixel widths that cannot shrink.
166	- Any wide block (the table) either scrolls inside its own `overflow-x:auto` container or restructures (cards) below a breakpoint. The page body never scrolls sideways.
167	- The off-canvas drawer must be `display:none` or `aria-hidden` when closed, not parked off-screen, so the gate does not read it as an escaping element.
168	- Watch the small ones: the mock leaked 4px at desktop widths. A stray `100vw`, a negative margin, or a `min-w` that will not shrink is usually the cause. The gate catches these; do not ship them.
169	
170	Layout grammar (enforced by the Part 2 gate): grid for two-dimensional regions, flex for single-axis runs, no nested flex faking a grid, tokens instead of literal colours or pixel values in any hand-written CSS.
171	
172	## The off-canvas gate refinement (constitution to-do)
173	
174	Running the responsive auditor on this rich layout surfaced that off-canvas navigation (the standard mobile drawer) reads as `element-escape` because a translated-off-screen element has a negative x. The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. Before the capstone run, the Part 5 spec and auditor/gate need an exemption: an element that is `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `aria-hidden="true"` (a deliberately-hidden drawer) is not an escape. Decide the rule, write it into `harness/responsive-spec.md`, and update the auditor and the gate together (they stay two independent encodings of one spec). This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.
175	
176	## Content (example data, hero-agency specific)
177	
178	Reuse the roster from the mock (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian) with their power classes (Aerial, Energy, Psionic, Tech, Mutant, Cosmic, Enhanced), power index (0-100), status (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), clearance tier, mission counts, and success rates. Mark it plainly as example data. The specifics (threat tiers, power classes, clearance) are the detail that makes this a real console rather than a generic CRUD table.

nav: Threats          lucideShieldAlert
nav: Recruit          lucideUserPlus

## Build guidelines

- Top bar controls: `hlmBtn` (icon buttons), `hlmInput` (search), `hlm-tooltip` on icon-only buttons, `hlm-avatar` for the account chip.
- Stat tiles and hero cards: `hlm-card` and its parts; `hlm-badge` for trends and classes; `hlm-avatar` for hero portraits.
- Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.
- Detail: `hlm-tabs`, `hlm-avatar`, `hlm-badge`; the edit form uses `hlm-field` + `hlm-label` + `hlmInput` + `hlm-select` + `hlm-switch` + a textarea; retire uses `hlm-dialog`. Toast/feedback via whatever spartan provides (sonner/toast) or a small local one.
- Icons everywhere via `<ng-icon>` per the scheme above.

- Each routed feature screen (Dashboard, Roster, HeroDetail, Recruit) gets a ViewModel: an `@Injectable` service holding all logic and state as signals, unit-testable with no DOM.

- The off-canvas drawer must be `display:none` or `aria-hidden` when closed, not parked off-screen, so the gate does not read it as an escaping element.

Layout grammar (enforced by the Part 2 gate): grid for two-dimensional regions, flex for single-axis runs, no nested flex faking a grid, tokens instead of literal colours or pixel values in any hand-written CSS.

The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. Before the capstone run, the Part 5 spec and auditor/gate need an exemption: an element that is `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `aria-hidden="true"` (a deliberately-hidden drawer) is not an escape. Decide the rule, write it into `harness/responsive-spec.md`, and update the auditor and the gate together (they stay two independent encodings of one spec). This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.

## Content (example data, hero-agency specific)

Reuse the roster from the mock (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian) with their power classes (Aerial, Energy, Psionic, Tech, Mutant, Cosmic, Enhanced), power index (0-100), status (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), clearance tier, mission counts, and success rates. Base directory for this skill: D:\Repos\angular-jig\.claude\skills\house-style # House frontend conventions These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 5. **App stylesheets are layout only.** Every utility in `@apply` and every plain declaration in a stylesheet under `src/app`, and every class rule in `src/styles.css`, must be layout: display, flex and grid arrangement, gap, sizing, margin, position, overflow and text alignment (the full list is under "The layout list" below). Color, typography, border, radius, shadow, ring, opacity, transitions, cursor, custom properties and anything not on the list are appearance, and appearance lives in `libs/ui`. Padding is allowed in one place: the component's block root (`.roster`, `.roster--compact`, or `:host`), for the region's inset, and only when that element is not a primitive. Semantic tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions. Moving appearance onto a wrapper element, or removing a primitive's directive to keep its look, does not make it allowed. 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. ```html

``` ```css /* roster.css */ @reference "../../styles.css"; .roster { @apply grid gap-6 p-6; } .roster__header { @apply grid gap-1; } .roster__filters { @apply flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3; } .roster__label { @apply sr-only; } .roster__search { @apply w-full sm:w-64; } .roster__recruit { @apply ms-auto; } .roster__row { @apply flex items-center gap-2; } ``` Note what the stylesheet does not say. No rule picks a color, a font size, a weight or a radius: the title is `hlmH3`, the caption `hlmMuted`, the icon's color its `tone`, the retired state a badge variant. `p-6` sits on `.roster`, the block root, as the region's inset. `roster__search` and `roster__recruit` sit on primitives and apply only width and margin. When no existing variant gives the look you need (an input padded to make room for an icon, a quieter table cell, a rounded panel), add a variant to the primitive itself: edit the owned copy of its component in `libs/ui`, add the variant to its `cva` using semantic tokens only, and select it from the template with the input (``). `libs/ui` is the one place `cva` and utility strings in TypeScript belong; rule 6 applies to `src/app`. One variant serves every screen that needs the look, which is the point: a primitive's appearance is decided in one place, not re-decided at every call site. ### The layout list After any variant prefix (`sm:`, `hover:`, `dark:`) and a `!` marker are removed, these are layout. Anything else is appearance. - Display and box: `block`, `inline`, `inline-block`, `flex`, `inline-flex`, `grid`, `inline-grid`, `contents`, `hidden`, `sr-only`, `not-sr-only`, `box-border`, `box-content`. - Flex and grid: `flex-*`, `grow*`, `shrink*`, `basis-*`, `order-*`, `grid-cols-*`, `grid-rows-*`, `col-*`, `row-*`, `auto-cols-*`, `auto-rows-*`, `grid-flow-*`, `items-*`, `justify-*`, `content-*` (alignment), `self-*`, `place-*`, `gap-*`. - Sizing: `w-*`, `h-*`, `size-*`, `min-w-*`, `min-h-*`, `max-w-*`, `max-h-*`, `aspect-*`. - Margin: `m-*`, `mx-*`, `my-*`, `mt-*`, `mr-*`, `mb-*`, `ml-*`, `ms-*`, `me-*`, and negatives. - Position: `static`, `relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky`, `inset-*`, `top-*`, `right-*`, `bottom-*`, `left-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`, `z-*`. - Overflow and flow: `overflow-*`, `overscroll-*`, `truncate`, `text-ellipsis`, `text-clip`, `whitespace-*`, `break-*`, `text-left`, `text-center`, `text-right`, `text-start`, `text-end`, `text-justify`, `object-*`, `isolate`, `container`. - Padding: only on the block root. Plain declarations follow the same line: `display`, `flex*`, `grid*`, `gap`, sizing, `margin*`, `position`, `inset*`, `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left`, `z-index`, `overflow*`, `text-overflow`, `white-space`, `word-break`, `overflow-wrap`, `text-align`, `object-fit`, `object-position`, `isolation`, `order`, `align-*`, `justify-*`, `place-*`. `color: var(--sidebar-primary)` is appearance. ### Where appearance comes from - **A primitive's look:** its `variant`/`size` inputs; when none fits, a new variant on the primitive in `libs/ui` (above). - **Text:** a typography directive from `@spartan-ng/helm/typography`: `hlmH1` to `hlmH4`, `hlmP`, `hlmLead`, `hlmLarge`, `hlmSmall`, `hlmMuted`, `hlmCode`, `hlmBlockquote`, `hlmUl`. `

Tones: `default` (inherits the surrounding color), `muted`, `primary`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`. Size icons with `ng-icon`'s `size` input or `size-*` in the stylesheet. - **A region's inset:** padding on the block root. - **Status colors:** `success` and `warning` exist as tokens next to `destructive`; use them through a primitive's variant, a tone, or a typography variant, never from the app stylesheet. ## The sealed control vocabulary Helm primitives are copied into `libs/ui`, so the set of primitives this repo owns is exactly what that directory ships. content.text:
The shell and theme are in place. `ng build` compiles, and the lint, contrast, boot, interaction, responsive and unit-test gates pass.

**One deviation from the spec:** the light-theme `--primary-foreground` and `--sidebar-primary-foreground` are `#241a05`, not the spec's `#ffffff`. White on `#d8891a` is 2.8:1, and the contrast gate fails it. `#241a05` is the dark theme's ink, and it passes at about 6:1. If you want white kept, the amber itself would need to darken.

**What was built**
- **Theme (`src/styles.css`):** the spec palette is mapped onto the spartan tokens in both `:root` and `:root.dark`. The full `--sidebar*` set is kept. I added `--info` and `--info-foreground`, since the palette lists info. `--sidebar-muted` has no spartan token and nothing consumes it, so I didn't define it.
- **Shell (`app.ts` / `app.html` / `app.css`):** `hlm-sidebar` with header, nav (six items), and an "Example data only." footer, inside `hlmSidebarWrapper` and `main[hlmSidebarInset]`. The drawer is the sidebar's own sheet, which only renders while open.
- **Topbar (`src/app/topbar/`):** the sidebar trigger, a breadcrumb, a search form, notifications, the theme toggle, and an avatar. The icon buttons use `hlmTooltip`, which is the selector the primitive actually declares.
- **Theme logic (`src/app/app-shell.view-model.ts`):** a component-scoped `AppShellViewModel`. It toggles `.dark` on `<html>`, persists the choice to localStorage, and follows `prefers-color-scheme` until the user chooses. It is provided by `Topbar`, since that component injects it, which the lint rule requires.
- **Routes:** seven lazy routes: dashboard, `roster`, `detail/:id`, missions, threats, recruit, settings. The old `heroes` path is now `roster`; the component file is unchanged. Missions, threats, recruit and settings are minimal placeholders.

**Things to know**
- **Bundle budget warning:** the initial bundle is 562 kB against a 500 kB budget. It is a warning and the build still succeeds. I did not change `angular.json`; raising the budget is your call.
- **`check:wiring` can't run:** `package.json` points at `harness/counter/check-wiring.mjs`, which is not in the repo. I checked by hand that every public `AppShellViewModel` member is read by `topbar.html`.
- **Search** navigates to `/roster?q=…`. The roster screen doesn't read `q` yet.
- **Dark mode** is verified by the gates, not by looking at it in a browser. The toggle, persistence and system-preference fallback are not exercised by any check I ran.
- **Gate limit:** the contrast gate skips the amber focus rings, because they are 8-digit hex with alpha and it can't read them. They are unverified.
- **Not touched:** `tsconfig.json` and `.claude/settings.json` were already modified before I started, and I left them as they were. A hook blocked a shell read of `tsconfig.json` during this work.
